notes.title: Individual degree plans and progression
notes.summary: New students attend orientation and prepare an advisor-approved four-year plan during their first semester before subsequent registration. Major benchmarks are reviewed periodically; falling behind requires advising, and continuing after unmet benchmarks needs dean approval. A major change requires an approved new plan. Ten semesters or 130 credits triggers mandatory advising, with approved modified plans for exceptional or extended programs. Transfer credits count through the stated credit-to-semester rule, while AP/IB and pre-matriculation high-school college credit do not count toward that limit. Summer/winter credits count, but those terms do not add semesters.

notes.title: Registration and conditional credit loads
notes.summary: University limits without college approval are 20 fall/spring credits (16 before classes begin), eight per summer session and four in winter. A stricter college limit still applies. Schedule adjustment is normally ten class days in fall/spring, four in six-week summer sessions and one in three-week sessions. Afterward, adds require a college exception; drops are normally limited to four credits, with the stated whole-course exception and W/attempt consequences. These scheduling conditions do not add degree courses.

notes.title: Conditional graduate-course enrollment
notes.summary: For undergraduate credit, 600–897 courses except 799 require prior department and instructor approval and must be outside 12-week programs. They do not automatically grant graduate admission or double credit. Graduate-credit-only enrollment has separate college, department, instructor and Graduate School approvals, junior standing, GPA 3.0, B- prerequisites and an approved plan; those credits do not count toward the bachelor degree. Combined-degree exceptions require their own approved program.

notes.title: Conditional interinstitutional enrollment
notes.summary: External degree credit requires advance dean approval. DC Consortium participation requires degree-seeking enrollment, junior standing, space and host prerequisites; comparable UMD courses are excluded. USM interinstitutional participation requires at least sophomore standing, space and host criteria; UMD Global Campus is excluded for UMD undergraduates. Approved participating credit may be resident credit, but no automatic course equivalence or waived prerequisite is inferred.

notes.title: Academic standing and conditional continuation
notes.summary: Cumulative GPA below 2.0 leads to probation. At 60 or more credits, failure to recover after the probationary semester leads to dismissal, with the stated winter/summer recovery exceptions. Below 60 credits, continued probation requires semester GPA 2.0 and, for full-time students, at least nine completed credits as defined by the policy; cumulative 2.0 is required at the semester reaching 60 credits. Probation/reinstatement registration changes require advising approval. Reinstatement depends on the Faculty Petition Board, not an automatic entitlement.

notes.title: Conditional academic clemency
notes.summary: A returning first-bachelor student after at least five calendar years away may seek one-time clemency by the end of the first return semester. Subject to satisfactory completion, up to 16 attempted D/F credits can be excluded from cumulative GPA. They remain on the transcript and in repeat/Latin-honors accounting, and cannot satisfy degree requirements. No individual approval is presumed.

notes.title: ARHU upper-level cohort and first-year condition
notes.summary: The college plans page identifies 39 upper-level credits for students entering ARHU from fall 2024, separately from its earlier 45-credit statement. It names the living-learning exemptions to first-semester ARHU158; the current catalog describes the exemption as a two-year living-learning program. The linked HCAI plan retains 120 total/39 upper-level credits and conditional ARHU158 or equivalent.

notes.title: ARHU declaration procedure
notes.summary: Adding or declaring an ARHU major requires a departmental advising meeting and academic plan, World Language Placement under the published exemption rules, and an ARHU advising appointment to complete the change.

notes.title: ARHU conditional exception procedure
notes.summary: Academic exceptions are considered only in rare or extraordinary cases and are not guaranteed. Late adds and time conflicts require instructor support; grading-mode changes, repeat requests and overloads require the appropriate college process. Requests above 20 fall/spring credits are not considered before classes begin. A permitted petition is not approval of an academic substitution or eligibility waiver.

notes.title: ARHU conferral and commencement distinction
notes.summary: Apply for graduation by final-semester schedule adjustment and seek both departmental and college audits before final registration. Degree conferral requires all academic requirements and outstanding university obligations to be completed. The page describes May 2026 ceremonies and conditional summer-completer petitions; those event dates are not generalized to a future cohort or counted as academic requirements.

notes.title: CMNS grades, residence and repeat rules
notes.summary: CMNS requires C- or better in major courses unless the curriculum specifies otherwise, major and cumulative GPA 2.0, and generally D- in General Education except C- in Academic Writing. Final-30 residence rules retain approved exceptions. Prior permission is needed for outside coursework, and CMNS prohibits repeating elsewhere a course already attempted at UMD, including a W. The published college load is 17 fall/spring, four winter and eight in one summer session; overload is conditional. These college rules are not replaced by the less restrictive university maximum.

notes.title: CMNS exceptions and external final credits
notes.summary: Rare/extraordinary exceptions require a documented college petition. Within the final 30 credits, external domestic work needs the final-credit exception and, when applicable, permission to enroll; at most six non-internship/non-study-abroad credits may be outside UMD with advance approval. Study abroad has its separate final-credit/SACA forms. First-semester students are ineligible for overload; listed GPA thresholds name other majors, so no AI-specific threshold is invented. The page’s phrase “two repeats” is followed by “third attempt”; the catalog and college academic page explicitly establish two total attempts, which remain the recorded ordinary limit.

notes.title: Published limited-enrollment scope
notes.summary: The inspected admissions LEP list names Computer Science and other specified programs but does not list either AI degree. It states admitted applicants who did not choose an LEP are admitted to their selected major. This bounded current list does not authorize importing Computer Science gateway courses into the separate BSAI or HCAI degree, and does not invent an unpublished internal-change procedure.
